nodes.label: VibeOffice 갭 분석 — 현재 구현 vs 목표 명세
AI Office 업무 경계·산출물 파이프라인 수정 결과
02. Users and Jobs To Be Done
L1 Contract Harness
nodes.rationale: Validates state-machine invariants with mocked models via in-process function calls; DB direct writes allowed only in setup, so it can test invariants cheaply before system-level layers are trusted.

nodes.label: L2 System E2E Harness
nodes.rationale: Uses a deterministic fake model adapter instead of mocking run_agent, forcing HTTP-only entry points and a real worker process so that tool execution, storage, and lease/heartbeat paths are exercised for real; direct DB writes are banned via AST check to prevent tests from faking system behavior.

nodes.label: L3 Agent Eval Harness
nodes.rationale: Evaluates actual model quality (not just system mechanics) via Golden Tasks run against real models, since cost prevents automatic CI execution and results need repeats to measure reliability (pass^k).

nodes.label: Golden Task (5종)
nodes.rationale: Reduced from 10 to 5 canonical end-to-end scenarios to keep local verification feasible while still covering full pipeline, vague-input intake, bugfix, Korean office docs, and QA-bounce-loop cases.

nodes.label: RunLog Schema (JSONL)
nodes.rationale: Adopted from Inspect AI's task/manifest/samples/results/reductions structure so that rescoring can happen against stored logs without re-invoking paid models.

nodes.label: Deterministic Fake Model Adapter
nodes.rationale: Only fakes the OpenRouter HTTP call, keyed by sha256 hash of messages+tools, so real tool execution/parsing/storage code paths run; a prompt change breaks the hash lookup deliberately (VCR-style re-record + diff review) to surface drift instead of hiding it.

nodes.label: pass@k metric
nodes.rationale: Measures capability ceiling (at least one success in k tries), borrowed from tau-bench.

nodes.label: pass^k metric (reliability)
nodes.rationale: Operational definition of 'trustworthy' is pass^3 (all k succeed), not pass@1 — chosen because a system you can delegate to must succeed consistently, not just occasionally.

nodes.label: LLM Judge Calibration (Cohen's kappa gate)
nodes.rationale: Raw agreement percentage is rejected because it's inflated by chance; kappa<0.4 signals an ambiguous rubric to fix, kappa>0.6 required before a judge scorer counts as a trustworthy metric — borrowed from MT-Bench findings on judge position/verbosity/self-preference bias.

nodes.label: SWE-bench FAIL_TO_PASS / PASS_TO_PASS
nodes.rationale: Adopted to close the gap where fixture-based checks only verify 'code was produced' — FAIL_TO_PASS proves the bug was actually fixed, PASS_TO_PASS proves nothing else broke; must be paired with blast_radius/diff_relevance because tests can pass without genuinely fixing the issue (arxiv 2503.15223).

nodes.label: Inspect AI Task/Solver/Scorer + rescore
nodes.rationale: Rescoring stored RunLogs with a revised scorer avoids re-calling paid models every time a rubric is tweaked, which would double cost on every iteration.

nodes.label: Mutation Testing kill-rate gate (>=90%)
nodes.rationale: Disabling each gate condition one at a time and requiring the test suite to catch it (90%+ kill rate) is used to prove invariant tests are not merely present but actually enforce the invariant.

nodes.label: Docker-only Sandbox Isolation (B3)
nodes.rationale: gVisor/Firecracker/microVM roadmap intentionally dropped as out of scope (deployment-time concern) — Docker + resource limits (network=none, 2GiB mem, 2 CPU, 512 PID, timeouts, non-root, cap-drop=ALL) is judged sufficient to test that an agent cannot escape its workspace locally.

nodes.label: VibeOffice (Guided Product-to-Code Workspace)
nodes.rationale: Positioned as connecting rough non-technical ideas to Codex/Claude Code handoff via minimized questions, scope control, quick draft mockups, and structured artifacts — explicitly not a full autonomous dev tool, not multi-stack, not a marketing pitch about many agents.

nodes.label: 6-Department Product Pipeline (Planning/Design/Architecture/Build/QA/Shipping)
nodes.rationale: Fixed department order (unlike the 8-department dynamic GLM routing used elsewhere) is required because product gates only make sense with a stable sequence; this is a deliberate departure from the runtime's normal dynamic routing.

nodes.label: Handoff Envelope (versioned contract)
nodes.rationale: Department handoff is defined as a version-pinned input/output contract rather than a chat summary specifically so the next department cannot silently drift scope by referencing an unapproved draft.

nodes.label: project-blueprint.json
nodes.rationale: Serves as the machine-verifiable source of truth for Must/Later/Out scope; PRD.md must match its IDs/values or it is treated as an error, preventing the human doc and machine doc from silently diverging.

nodes.label: PRD.md (single human-facing spec)
nodes.rationale: Standard mode deliberately collapses PRODUCT_BRIEF/MVP_SCOPE/REQUIREMENTS/DECISIONS/OKR/RISK into one PRD document to avoid duplicated editing surfaces; derived docs are only generated for external/enterprise/regulated needs and are never edited directly.

nodes.label: Gate B — Scope
nodes.rationale: Must count is bounded to 3-5 specifically to prevent beginner scope creep given short team timelines; combos like auth+AI+file+realtime+payment together trigger a warning.

nodes.label: Gate PE — Product Execution Baseline
nodes.rationale: Requires every Must requirement to trace to a PRD section+acceptance criteria+task+test, and blocks handoff on any deferred Build-blocking decision or unmitigated High/Critical risk — designed so PRD derivation stays decision-traceable without adding a new blueprint field.

nodes.label: Handoff Readiness Grades H0-H5
nodes.rationale: Standard export target is H4 (working mockup+mock+traceability+test scaffold) rather than H5, because full build+smoke+evidence+checkpoint is reserved for the optional quality mode — balancing beginner speed against completeness.

nodes.label: Review Finding structure (severity/category/ownerDepartment/autoFixable)
nodes.rationale: Findings route to a single owning department instead of triggering a full regeneration, so a bad plan doesn't get amplified through design/architecture/code before being caught.

nodes.label: Stale Propagation Rules
nodes.rationale: Different change types (target user, Must, tech stack, copy) invalidate different artifact sets — minimizing blast radius so a copy tweak doesn't force full regeneration of architecture docs.

nodes.label: Repeat-finding loop break (2x rule)
nodes.rationale: If the same finding recurs twice, automatic fixing stops and escalates to upstream-conflict investigation or human judgment — an explicit circuit breaker against infinite agent rework loops.

nodes.label: CLAUDE.md (Claude Code handoff file)
nodes.rationale: Recommended to use @-imports of AGENTS.md, NEXT_ACTION.md, PROJECT_STATUS.md, PRD.md, TASKS.md, TEST_PLAN.md, decision/risk registers so Claude Code loads full context without a human re-explaining it.

nodes.label: NEXT_ACTION.md (single vertical slice)
nodes.rationale: Deliberately scoped to exactly one vertical slice with explicit in/out/done/rollback so the coding agent doesn't re-plan the whole product on first run.

nodes.label: PROJECT_STATUS.md (fact not plan)
nodes.rationale: Explicitly documents current fact (Working/Partial/Not-implemented/Known-issues) rather than plan, to be kept separate from planning docs per the 'don't mix plan and current-state in one document' prohibition.

nodes.label: TaskContract (execution-layer permission boundary)
nodes.rationale: VibeOffice's vo_* tables and S4 internal build reuse only apps/api/policy.py's validate_command and never enter the Job queue/TaskContract system — meaning the product layer and execution layer remain unconnected despite the architecture diagram implying the link.

nodes.label: 8-Department Company Boundaries (department-boundaries.json)
nodes.rationale: Distinct from VibeOffice's fixed 6 product departments — the 8 company departments use dynamic GLM routing per request instead of a fixed pipeline, which the gap analysis flags as a coming conflict since fixed product gates and dynamic routing don't mix.

nodes.label: GLM Dynamic Department Routing
nodes.rationale: Removed all static task-profile keyword hardcoding (task-profiles.json now has 0 static profiles) so GLM decides departments/workers/skills/final-owner per request dynamically, based on live department ownership and deliverable standards.

nodes.label: FINAL.md Integration Gate
nodes.rationale: Fixes a diagnosed failure (TASK-008) where worker/department drafts conflicted and were passed to team-lead review unmerged with zero write_file calls; now drafts must be saved as real files, a designated final owner merges them into one FINAL.md, and lead review inspects the actual file, not a DB summary.

nodes.label: deliverable-standards.json (8 artifact-type standards)
nodes.rationale: Chat replies are explicitly not accepted as deliverables; filename, required sections, and review rules per artifact type enforce file-existence + section + source + format QA.

nodes.label: GOAL→FEATURE→REQUIREMENT→FLOW→SCREEN→DATA/API→TASK→TEST→EVIDENCE chain
nodes.rationale: Evaluates artifacts by whether they interlock into real implementation/verification rather than by artifact count; drift is defined as the gap between project-blueprint.json (plan) and current-state.json (actual).

nodes.label: Vertical Slices S1-S6 (Intake→Export→Conversational UI)
nodes.rationale: Explicit rule not to start S6 (conversational layer, office UI, direct visual edit) before S1-S5 finish, and not to build avatar/office theater before the product pipeline works — ordering enforces substance over surface polish.

nodes.label: Manifest (trymanifest.dev)
nodes.rationale: Positioned as a strategy/continuity layer in front of AI builders (Lovable, Claude Code, Cursor, Bolt, Replit, GitHub Codespaces); VibeOffice's differentiation is shipping an actual project folder and executable draft instead of only builder prompts.

nodes.label: Replit Agent
nodes.rationale: Strong on generation speed, instant runtime, deployment convenience — VibeOffice differentiates as a neutral pre-build layer stabilizing intent/scope/artifacts rather than competing on the implementation environment itself.

nodes.label: v0 / Lovable / Bolt
nodes.rationale: Risk to avoid: stacking plausible-looking screens without first fixing product scope and data flow.

nodes.label: OpenClaw
nodes.rationale: To avoid: granting full computer access, always-on autonomy, unlimited community skills from the start.

nodes.label: Hermes Agent
nodes.rationale: Self-improvement deferred until approval/verification/rollback are in place — sequencing lesson borrowed directly.

nodes.label: JENSEn OS
nodes.rationale: Positioning caution: lead with 'turns an idea into a first buildable version' rather than 'AI company operating system'.

nodes.label: MetaGPT / ChatDev / CrewAI
nodes.rationale: To avoid: making long CEO/CTO/developer dialogue the core experience — only decisions, rationale, artifacts, and review results should surface to the user.
